Nora — great to get the MAP. I reviewed v0.3 and sketched owners below so we have direct points of contact.

Assigned owners (dev + delivery):
- SDK / client integration (Java/TS): marissa_cole — will prepare an SDK snapshot and sample app by 7/6
- Auth / token refresh / KMS flow: sean_gallagher — will provide a token-flow diagram and proposed KMS integration by 7/2

Prelim blockers we flagged:
- Streaming: certificate rotation + long-lived websocket reconnection semantics (might need a short-lived heartbeat)

- Tool-calling: we need to agree on a retry/backoff strategy for synchronous tool calls to avoid double-execution

1) Tech owners to post short bullet plans to the shared Drive folder (link below) by EOD Mon 6/29
2) Quick cadence: 30-min weekly tech checkpoint Wednesdays 11:00-11:30 PT starting 7/1 (accept if that works)
3) Canary plan: Marissa to propose a canary checklist (smoke tests + perf targets) by 7/6; we’ll lock a pilot window 7/20-7/24 if green

Thanks — posting a quick tech update and a few asks. Quoted for context:

> Karthik — aim to validate streaming handshake at low latency by 7/10

What we’ve validated so far:
- Basic SDKs (Java + TS) can do non-streamed generation with our hosted endpoints; sample app runs locally.
- Streaming prototype works for short sessions (<30s) but we see two issues under longer sessions:
  - 1) intermittent reconnection after ~10m idle when Acme’s NAT gateway resets TCP. Need an explicit reconnect + resume token.
  - 2) token refresh is currently synchronous in the client; for streaming we need an async refresh that swaps the auth header without dropping the session (or use a short-lived resumable JWT).

Proposed mitigations / action items:
- Marissa to deliver sdk-streaming-proposal.patch with resumable session handshake changes and an example of incremental token swap — due 7/6 (attachment).
- Sean to provide auth-token-flow-diagram.png documenting KMS wrap/unwrap and suggested token TTL — due 7/2.
- Monica to confirm router adapter semantics for idempotency keys and dedupe behavior by 7/8.

I also attached sdk-benchmarks.csv with a quick perf run on g4dn-like instances showing throughput at different batch sizes — this will feed the canary smoke tests.

If we hit the NAT re-auth issue, short-term we can recommend a keepalive heartbeat from the browser/edge to keep connections open, but long-term we’ll implement the resumable handshake.

Marissa Cole
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sdk-streaming-proposal.patch, sdk-benchmarks.csv

Appreciate the quick turnaround, team — summarizing final agreements and timeline so Acme has a single source of truth for the MAP milestones before we lock the first canary window.

MAP milestones & owners (final):
- 7/02: Auth diagram + KMS approach (owner: sean_gallagher) — deliverable: auth-token-flow-diagram.png
- 7/06: SDK resumable-handshake + sample app + canary checklist (owner: marissa_cole) — deliverable: sdk-streaming-proposal.patch, sdk-benchmarks.csv
- 7/08: Router adapter contract + idempotency plan (owner: monica_patel) — deliverable: router-adapter-spec.md (to be posted to Drive)
- 7/10: Streaming handshake validation in staging (owner: marissa_cole + seans) — pass/fail smoke tests
- 7/20: Canary rollout start (small cohort) — scope: 100 sessions/day, monitoring + rollback plan

Acceptance criteria for canary:
- Median p95 token latency < 250ms
- No >1% connection error rate over 24h window
- Tool calls must expose idempotency-key behavior with documented semantics

If the above milestones are green, we’ll proceed with the pilot window 7/20-7/24 and then fast-follow to broader pilot.

Action items assigned in HubSpot: HS-12345678 -> DEAL-4381 MAP tasks. I’ll convert the Drive checklist into an internal README for the canary run so CS (Monica) can run acceptance tests on day 0.

Thanks everyone — please reply only for blocker-level changes. Otherwise I’ll treat the items as agreed and update the MAP spreadsheet.

—Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
